I will keep things simple and steady this year. Where I farm in Quzhou County, the safest path for me is still the usual wheat and summer maize rotation on the same land. I know this pattern, the machines fit it, the market is clear, and it spreads my risk better than trying something fancy. At my age, I care more about stable output and work I can manage on time than chasing a crop with higher risk. So I will finish the winter wheat that is already in the field, then after harvest I will sow summer maize right away.

For management, I will not make it complicated. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want better stand, better yield, and fewer problems than old saved seed. I will put most fertilizer into nitrogen, but I will still use phosphorus and potassium so the crop does not grow weak. For wheat, I will irrigate a few key times because spring water matters a lot here. After wheat harvest, I will seed maize quickly, mostly with no-tillage, because that saves time and keeps moisture. I will spray only as needed for the common diseases, insects, and weeds, because too many sprays waste money. My whole plan is to keep the land fully used, keep the work schedule tight, and aim for dependable grain yield.
